findings.claim: Tableau column drop frames are only as wide as the cards, so the ~5 pt gutter between two columns belongs to no column: a legal drag released there is silently refused (card snaps back, Moves unchanged) even though the dragged card is rendered centred on the finger and visibly overlaps the intended column by ~45% of its width. An earlier fix extended these frames vertically to the bottom of the tableau; horizontally they still do not tile.

repro: fresh install + launch (no daily HUD, portrait)
tap Deal # (196,175), clear the field, enter 10004, tap Play
drag (321,612) -> (28,700)   [10H onto JC, col0 = 8 cards, Moves 1]
drag (28,620) -> (224,700)   [JC+10H run to col4, col0 bottom is now 4D, Moves 2]
drag (175,642) -> (274,296)  [8S to free cell 1, exposing 5S at col3 bottom, Moves 3]
drag (175,612) -> (52,700)   [release 5S in the gap between col0 and col1: card snaps back, Moves STAYS 3]
drag (175,612) -> (48,700)   [same drag released 4 pt further left: 5S lands on 4D in col0, Moves 4]

findings.note: Reproduced with two different cards (JD legal only on col1, 5S legal only on col0): BOTH are refused at x=52, which proves the gutter belongs to neither column rather than resolving to the nearer one. No drop-target highlight is drawn during a drag, so the only feedback is the snap-back. Cheap fix: make each column's drop frame span its full pitch (or resolve a release to the column with the greatest overlap / nearest centre). Not a move-count corruption: the refused release correctly counts no move.
